FLASHCARD SET · AGES 2 YEARS

Animals & Sounds flashcards.

Twenty big animal cards for toddlers who love to make some noise. Say the sound together, name the animal and then listen for it on your street, at the park or on a farm visit.

These cards belong to Toddler 5 on the Kiddo School learning path.

HOW TO USE THESE CARDS

Four ways that work.

You do not need a plan or a printer schedule. Pick one idea, try it for two minutes and see what happens.

  1. 01

    Name and make the sound

    Show one card and say the animal name, then the sound: cow — moo! Let your toddler copy. Getting it "wrong" is still learning, so laugh together and try again.

  2. 02

    Play find the animal

    Lay out three or four cards and ask which one moos, or which one has wings. Let your toddler point, grab or hop on the right one — any answer that shows they looked counts.

  3. 03

    Take it outside

    After the dog card, watch for a real dog on your walk. A sound you heard on a card is twice as exciting when it walks past your garden gate.

  4. 04

    One or two cards is plenty

    Stop while it is still fun. Two minutes of animal sounds today works better than twenty minutes tomorrow.

      Dog Flashcard for Toddlers

      Most toddlers meet a dog before they can say much more than "dog", which is exactly why this card works. The picture is big and clear, and the sound is one your toddler already loves to try.

      Teaching tips

      What this card teaches

      Names the animal your toddler greets first on every walk, woof included.

      Make the sound

      Be the dog for a minute — pat the floor, wag, and woof twice.

      What kids learn from it

      First animal words grow fastest from sounds the mouth can already make.

      Print it like this

      Print on card — this one gets carried everywhere, including to windows.

      Grown-up tip

      Wait three seconds after the card appears; that silence invites the woof.

      Teach it, step by step

      This card belongs to a real class — open the Animals and Sounds for 2-Year-Olds class on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · ANIMALS & SOUNDS · AGES 2 YEARS

      Cat Flashcard for Toddlers

      A cat says meow, and many toddlers say it back long before they can name the animal. The pointy ears and whiskers give you plenty to point at and name together.

      Teaching tips

      What this card teaches

      Gives the soft neighbour next door a name your toddler can say.

      Make the sound

      Paw a pompom across the floor, meowing politely after each pounce.

      What kids learn from it

      Gentle hands practice — soft voices and soft touches arrive together here.

      Print it like this

      Choose matte paper; the whiskers read clearer without lamp glare.

      Grown-up tip

      Whisper the meow first — quiet games stretch a toddler's attention longest.

      Teach it, step by step

      This card belongs to a real class — open the Animals and Sounds for 2-Year-Olds class on the Learning Path.

      Cow Flashcard for Toddlers

      The cow is usually the first animal sound toddlers master, because moo is long, slow and satisfying to say. Big animal, big voice — this card earns its keep fast.

      Teaching tips

      What this card teaches

      Puts a big friendly face on the moo your toddler already loves.

      Make the sound

      Pour pretend milk from a tiny jug, then moo a big slow thank-you.

      What kids learn from it

      Long sounds build breath control — moo is the perfect practice note.

      Print it like this

      Print at full size; cows deserve the biggest spot on the fridge.

      Grown-up tip

      Stretch the moo longer each round and let your toddler match you.

      Teach it, step by step

      This card belongs to a real class — open the Animals and Sounds for 2-Year-Olds class on the Learning Path.

      Duck Flashcard for Toddlers

      Quack is a funny word and a funny sound, and ducks are everywhere: parks, ponds, picture books. This card connects all of them in one go.

      Teaching tips

      What this card teaches

      Turns bath time and pond walks into vocabulary practice without trying.

      Make the sound

      Tuck a washcloth under your arm as a wing and quack-waddle to the door.

      What kids learn from it

      Silly walks plus sounds anchor words in the body, not just the ears.

      Print it like this

      Laminate this card — bathroom air curls ordinary paper fast.

      Grown-up tip

      Ask the duck a question in quack and pause for the answer.

      Teach it, step by step

      This card belongs to a real class — open the Animals and Sounds for 2-Year-Olds class on the Learning Path.

      One word, two lessons

      The duck quacks here with its sound; over in Look & Learn the same yellow duckling waddles — card 03 of a fifteen-card deck where every picture has its own move.

      Sheep Flashcard for Toddlers

      Baa is another easy early sound, and the sheep's woolly coat gives you something extra to touch and name — soft, fluffy, white. Simple card, big payoff.

      Teaching tips

      What this card teaches

      Hands your toddler the word for the fluffiest voice on the farm.

      Make the sound

      Baa at every staircase step — up loud, down soft, landing at the bottom bleating.

      What kids learn from it

      Loud and quiet versions teach that volume is something voices choose.

      Print it like this

      Extra copies recommended; baa-ing toddlers wear cards out fast.

      Grown-up tip

      Try one deliberate wrong baa and wait for the gentle fix.

      Teach it, step by step

      This card belongs to a real class — open the Animals and Sounds for 2-Year-Olds class on the Learning Path.

      Pig Flashcard for Toddlers

      The pig's curly tail and round snout make it easy to spot, and oink is a silly sound toddlers love to repeat. Expect this one to be requested again and again.

      Teaching tips

      What this card teaches

      Celebrates the messiest farm friend with a sound made for snorty noses.

      Make the sound

      Sniff the soap, the fruit bowl and your elbow, then oink triumphantly.

      What kids learn from it

      Nose noises give snorters and sniffers their turn at speech practice.

      Print it like this

      Tape it low at toddler eye level, fridge door height.

      Grown-up tip

      Oink between real chores; housework makes a fine backstage rhythm.

      Teach it, step by step

      This card belongs to a real class — open the Animals and Sounds for 2-Year-Olds class on the Learning Path.

      Horse Flashcard for Toddlers

      A big, gentle-looking horse with a long tail to point at. The sound is a fun challenge — lots of toddlers start with a lip trill before "neigh" arrives, and both are fine.

      Teaching tips

      What this card teaches

      Names the gentle giant that gallops through picture books and paddocks.

      Make the sound

      Bounce a toy horse across the table, neighing whenever it clears a mug fence.

      What kids learn from it

      Rhythm rides along with gallop beats, and beats help words stick.

      Print it like this

      Thick card only; tabletop landings dent flimsy paper.

      Grown-up tip

      Neigh ends on a wobble — practise the wobble; it is hilarious.

      Teach it, step by step

      This card belongs to a real class — open the Animals and Sounds for 2-Year-Olds class on the Learning Path.

      Chicken Flashcard for Toddlers

      Chickens turn up all over: books, songs, farms and breakfast. This card gives the word and the cluck, and breakfast eggs give you a real-world link for free.

      Teaching tips

      What this card teaches

      Explains where breakfast begins, one busy clucking bird at a time.

      Make the sound

      Peck fingertips across the table, bok-bok-bokking until every dot is dinner.

      What kids learn from it

      Fast repeated sounds sharpen listening for the small differences between words.

      Print it like this

      Keep it in the kitchen — clucks pair nicely with actual breakfast.

      Grown-up tip

      Answer every cluck with one back; conversations, even cluck ones, build talk.

      Teach it, step by step

      This card belongs to a real class — open the Animals and Sounds for 2-Year-Olds class on the Learning Path.

      Rooster Flashcard for Toddlers

      The rooster stands tall with a big red comb, and cock-a-doodle-doo is the longest, silliest sound in the set. Most toddlers cannot say it all — the ones who try end up breathless laughing.

      Teaching tips

      What this card teaches

      Gives mornings a soundtrack your toddler can perform before anyone's awake.

      Make the sound

      Announce breakfast from the hallway in your loudest cock-a-doodle-do, then tiptoe in.

      What kids learn from it

      The longest animal sound in the set builds real breath stamina.

      Print it like this

      Half-size for the bedroom door — dawn performances need staging.

      Grown-up tip

      Save the loudest doo for special occasions; quiet mornings exist.

      Teach it, step by step

      This card belongs to a real class — open the Animals and Sounds for 2-Year-Olds class on the Learning Path.

      Frog Flashcard for Toddlers

      A bright green frog on the front of the card, and a "ribbit" that doubles as a great first jumping game. Frogs sit still, which makes them perfect for pointing and naming.

      Teaching tips

      What this card teaches

      Links a jump, a sound and a word into one giggly package.

      Make the sound

      Squat small, spring big, and land each ribbit on a different floor tile.

      What kids learn from it

      Jump-and-say pairs movement with speech, doubling the memory trace.

      Print it like this

      Print two copies and play matching snap on the kitchen floor.

      Grown-up tip

      Crouch lower for quieter ribbits; tiny frogs whisper too.

      Teach it, step by step

      This card belongs to a real class — open the Animals and Sounds for 2-Year-Olds class on the Learning Path.

      Lion Flashcard for Toddlers

      The lion gets the loudest sound in the set, and toddlers deliver roars with total commitment. The mane gives you an easy thing to name: big hair, big voice.

      Teaching tips

      What this card teaches

      Hands your toddler the biggest sound in the house, sized to fit.

      Make the sound

      Roar into a cardboard tube and hear the lion grow instantly louder.

      What kids learn from it

      Practising huge volume on purpose builds brave, controlled loud voices.

      Print it like this

      Borderless if your printer allows; manes hate white margins.

      Grown-up tip

      Ask whether today's lion is a sleepy one or a hungry one.

      Teach it, step by step

      This card belongs to a real class — open the Animals and Sounds for 2-Year-Olds class on the Learning Path.

      Elephant Flashcard for Toddlers

      Big ears, long trunk — the elephant is the easiest animal to spot on the card and the most fun to copy. The trumpet sound is strange and wonderful, and toddlers love pretending their arm is a trunk.

      Teaching tips

      What this card teaches

      Names the biggest land animal and the trumpet sound it talks with.

      Make the sound

      March a slow elephant line across the kitchen, pawooing at every cupboard.

      What kids learn from it

      Big animals deserve big sounds — this card makes loud feel friendly.

      Print it like this

      Strong paper only — this card leads the stampede to the fridge.

      Grown-up tip

      Elephants also rumble too low to hear; try a chest hum.

      Teach it, step by step

      This card belongs to a real class — open the Animals and Sounds for 2-Year-Olds class on the Learning Path.

      Monkey Flashcard for Toddlers

      Monkeys do what toddlers wish they could: climb everything and swing all day. The "ooh-ooh" sound is one of the easiest in the set, and the copy-me possibilities are endless.

      Teaching tips

      What this card teaches

      Gives climbing, swinging energy a word and a call of its own.

      Make the sound

      Hang a sock tail from your waistband and ooh-ooh across the kitchen.

      What kids learn from it

      Copying sounds back and forth is the first real conversation.

      Print it like this

      Choose card stock; this card gets grabbed mid-swing often.

      Grown-up tip

      Trade ooh-oohs until somebody giggles — turn-taking, mastered.

      Teach it, step by step

      This card belongs to a real class — open the Animals and Sounds for 2-Year-Olds class on the Learning Path.

      Owl Flashcard for Toddlers

      Owls are quiet night birds, and "hoot" is a soft, round sound that suits end-of-day play. The big eyes on the card give you something gentle to point at — eyes that watch the dark.

      Teaching tips

      What this card teaches

      Introduces the night bird whose sound is a whisper, not a shout.

      Make the sound

      Turn the lamp low, tuck under a blanket, and trade tiny hoos.

      What kids learn from it

      Quiet sounds teach listening — soft ears need practice too.

      Print it like this

      Small suits this one — the calm card of the whole set.

      Grown-up tip

      Hoo duels with two-year-olds always end in whispers. Accept it.

      Teach it, step by step

      This card belongs to a real class — open the Animals and Sounds for 2-Year-Olds class on the Learning Path.

      Bee Flashcard for Toddlers

      The bee card comes with a sound you can make with your lips — bzzz — and a built-in lesson in gentle hands. Bees are busy visitors to gardens and flowers, not chase-and-grab toys.

      Teaching tips

      What this card teaches

      Puts a face on the summertime buzz your toddler hears in the garden.

      Make the sound

      Buzz your finger through the air, landing softly on shoulder, nose, then knee.

      What kids learn from it

      Lip buzzing strengthens the exact muscles later words rely on.

      Print it like this

      Fresh from the printer at naptime, revealed at snack time.

      Grown-up tip

      Lips tingle when the buzz is right — point that out.

      Teach it, step by step

      This card belongs to a real class — open the Animals and Sounds for 2-Year-Olds class on the Learning Path.

      Snake Flashcard for Toddlers

      A long, curly snake and a long, curly sound — sssssss. This one is more breath than noise, which makes it a nice change from the loud cards and a sneaky bit of mouth-muscle practice.

      Teaching tips

      What this card teaches

      Makes the trickiest sound in the set feel like a game, not work.

      Make the sound

      Draw a long chalk line down the hall and hiss your way along it.

      What kids learn from it

      Long steady hisses exercise breath control from lips to belly.

      Print it like this

      A4 landscape suits a snake — they run wider than tall.

      Grown-up tip

      Whisper hisses count too; quiet snakes are still proper snakes.

      Teach it, step by step

      This card belongs to a real class — open the Animals and Sounds for 2-Year-Olds class on the Learning Path.

      Mouse Flashcard for Toddlers

      Small, quick and squeaky, the mouse is the opposite of the elephant — and comparing the two cards is a game in itself. Squeak is a tiny sound that tiny voices are brilliant at.

      Teaching tips

      What this card teaches

      Presents the smallest card in the set, squeak attached.

      Make the sound

      Tiptoe one lap of the table on squeaky feet, whisper-squeaking each corner.

      What kids learn from it

      High pitches stretch little ears into new listening territory.

      Print it like this

      Small on purpose — this card fits inside a pocket.

      Grown-up tip

      Squeak in super-slow motion once; the giggle buys five more rounds.

      Teach it, step by step

      This card belongs to a real class — open the Animals and Sounds for 2-Year-Olds class on the Learning Path.

      Donkey Flashcard for Toddlers

      The donkey has the funniest sound in the set — hee-haw — and toddlers find it irresistible precisely because it sounds broken. Expect dramatic performances.

      Teaching tips

      What this card teaches

      Delivers the farm's funniest sound, two notes and a built-in laugh.

      Make the sound

      Sing hee-HAW at the sink — low splash for hee, high splash for HAW.

      What kids learn from it

      Two-note sounds teach up and down, the first ideas in music.

      Print it like this

      Prop it by the bath; donkeys adore splash hour.

      Grown-up tip

      You call hee, they answer HAW — echo games stick hard.

      Teach it, step by step

      This card belongs to a real class — open the Animals and Sounds for 2-Year-Olds class on the Learning Path.

      Goat Flashcard for Toddlers

      Goats eat everything and say "maa" — a sound that sits somewhere between a sheep and a scream, which is why toddlers find goats so funny. The little beard is the detail to spot.

      Teaching tips

      What this card teaches

      Introduces the farm's cheekiest eater and the bleat that comes with it.

      Make the sound

      Nibble a paper grass blade, one tiny chew at a time, then maa.

      What kids learn from it

      Spotting near-identical sounds apart trains careful, discriminating ears.

      Print it like this

      Hang it beside the sheep card; bleats love company.

      Grown-up tip

      A head-wobble while bleating is optional but strongly recommended.

      Teach it, step by step

      This card belongs to a real class — open the Animals and Sounds for 2-Year-Olds class on the Learning Path.

      Bird Flashcard for Toddlers

      Birds are the animals your toddler hears every single day, usually before they spot them. This card turns "tweet" into a listening game that works anywhere, any time.

      Teaching tips

      What this card teaches

      Turns every window and garden tree into naming practice for free.

      Make the sound

      Flap your elbows down the hallway, tweeting at every doorframe you pass.

      What kids learn from it

      Daily birds outside turn one card into an endless hunt-and-name game.

      Print it like this

      Small and taped near the window the birds visit.

      Grown-up tip

      Real tweets outside beat any game — stop and listen together.

      Teach it, step by step
